client_requirements: Generate new unpredictable nonce per outstanding attempt; no password/cookie/device credentials on proof request.
Fetch only nonce proof through unauthenticated transport; reject redirects and unexpected response/schema/nonce/MAC.
Verify MAC locally using QR secret recovered through native device-owner authentication; bind completion to same selected frame and lock generation.
Only then create strict TLS transport with returned UUID/SPKI and authenticate original QR secret over TLS; only then enroll protected PHOTO device credential.
Preserve previous connection and protected data on cancellation, failure, backgrounding or stale completion.
If bootstrap proof unavailable, retain previous connection and report capability unavailable; do not use TOFU, weaken TLS or reassign BLE roles.

identity.spki_sha256: lowercasehex64 of already-loaded public TLS certificate SPKI
identity.url: explicit canonical HTTPS origin from INKY_STUDIO_PHOTO_ACCESS_URL; no path/query/fragment/userinfo

mac.key: UTF8 of existing generated16ASCIIalphanumeric bootstrap_password; no new secret/key is generated or stored
mac.message: ASCII inky-legacy-tls-proof-v1 then NUL; nonce32rawbytes; UUID16RFCbytes; SPKI32rawbytes; URL_UTF8_length_u16_big_endian; exact URL_UTF8 bytes
mac.normalization: Verify MAC over exact returned URL bytes after schema validation; never normalize URL before MAC

non_goals: No authority to claim factory, configure clock/country/WiFi, publish TLS identity or enroll the first factory PHOTO owner.
No permission to mint an owner from a media/device cookie.
Does not recover a QR secret already lost before protected storage.
server_requirements: Use only existing already-validated bootstrap_password; absent/custom/invalid format refuses.
Read durable credentials without create/migrate/chmod; exact current record must match loaded credentials while holding auth rotation lock.
Public identity comes from already-loaded public TLS certificate; never read identity/private-key files.
Use bounded global throttle, fixed unavailable responses, no secret logging, no cookie issuance or storage/authority mutations.
All existing enroll/device/invitation endpoints remain HTTPS-only; no forwarded-scheme trust.
